questions.question: 36 persons can do a work in 10 days, working 6 hours a day. In how many days will 24 persons, working 9 hours a day complete the work?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

36 persons can do a work in 10 days, working 6 hours a day.

24 persons, working 9 hours a day.

**Formula used:**

Work = Number of persons × Number of days × Number of hours per day

**Calculation:**

Total work by 36 persons:

Work = 36 × 10 × 6

⇒ Work = 2160 hours

Now, let the number of days required by 24 persons be D:

Work = 24 × D × 9

⇒ 2160 = 24 × D × 9

⇒ D = 2160 / (24 × 9)

⇒ D = 10

**∴ The correct answer is option 1.**

questions.question: A can complete a piece of work in 9 days. B and C can complete the same work in 12 days and 18 days respectively. If A, B, C work together, then in how many days will they complete the work?
questions.solution:
Given

A can finish a work in 9 days

B can finish a work in 12 days

C can finish a work in 18 days

Concept

Men × efficiency = work

Calculation

Work done by A in one day(A) = (1/9) ---- (1)

work done by B in one day(B) = 1/12 ---- (2)

work done by C in one day(C) = 1/18 ---- (3)

Adding (1), (2) and (3)

⇒ A + B + C = (1/9) + (1/12) + (1/18)

⇒ A + B + C = (4 + 3 + 2)/36

⇒ (A + B + C) = 9/36

⇒ (A + B + C) = 1/4

⇒ A + B + C = 1/4

1/4th work is done by A, B and C in one day. so, Total work done by A, B and C in 4 days.

∴ A, B and C finish the work together in 4 days.

Efficiency of A = 36/9 = 4

Efficiency of B = 36/12 = 3

Efficiency of A = 36/18 = 2

Together, work will be done in = 36/(4 + 3 + 2) = 4 days.

questions.question: At a construction site, Raju can paint a wall in 36 hours, while Angad can do the same work in 18 hours. Sumit can paint the same wall in 24 hours. In how much time can they paint the wall if they all work together?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total work = LCM of 36, 18, and 24 = 72 units.

Combined efficiency = (72 ÷ 36) + (72 ÷ 18) + (72 ÷ 24).

Combined efficiency = 2 + 4 + 3 = 9 units/hour.

Time taken together = Total Work ÷ Combined efficiency = 72 ÷ 9 = 8 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 8 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pipes & Cisterns

This concept is identical to Time & Work. Inlet pipes do positive work (filling), while outlet pipes do negative work (emptying). Net efficiency determines the total time to fill or empty the tank.

Work & Wages

Wages are always distributed in the direct ratio of the total work done by each individual. If multiple people work together for the same number of days, wages are distributed in the ratio of their individual efficiencies.

Alternate Day Work

When workers operate on alternate days, you must calculate the total work done in one complete cycle (e.g., 2 days for 2 workers). Multiply the cycle to get as close to the total work as possible before calculating the remaining days individually.

questions.question: Work done by 8 men is completed in 10 days. The same work can be completed in 12 days when done by 10 women. How many days will it take to complete when 4 men and 4 women are employed to perform the same job?
questions.solution:
**Given : **

Work done by 8 men is completed in 10 days.

Same work can be completed in 12 days when done by 10 women.

**Formula Used : **

M₁H₁D₁/W₁ = M₂H₂D₂/W₂

**Calculation : **

⇒ 8M × 10 = 10W × 12

⇒ 80M = 120W

⇒ M/W = 120/80 = 3/2

Total Work = 8 × 3 × 10 = 240

Now, 240 = (4M + 4W) × time

⇒ time = 240/(4 × 3 + 4 × 2)

⇒ time = 240/20 = 12 days

**∴ The correct answer is 12 days.**

questions.question: A can do a piece of work in 10 days, while A and B together can complete it in 2(1)/(2) days. How long will B alone take to complete the work?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A and B together can complete the work in 2(1)/(2) days.

A alone can complete the work in 10 days.

**Calculation:**

⇒ Work done by A each day = (1)/(10)

⇒ According to the question,

⇒ (1)/(10)+(1)/(B)=(2)/(5)

⇒ (1)/(B)=(2)/(5)-(1)/(10)

⇒ (1)/(B)=(4-1)/(10) = (3)/(10)

⇒ B = (10)/(3)

**Therefore, B alone will take (10)/(3) days to complete the work.**

questions.question: P and Q can do a piece of work in 14 days. Q and R together can do it in 21 days. If P is twice as good a workman as R, then in how many days Q alone can do the work?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Number of days P and Q take to do a piece of work = 14 days

Number of days Q and R take to do a work = 21 days

P is twice as good as workman as R

**Calculation:**

Let P, Q and R can do the work in x, y, and z days respectively.

Amount of work done by P, Q, and R in 1 day is 1/x, 1/y, and 1/z respectively.

According to the question,

⇒ (1)/(x)+(1)/(y)=(1)/(14) (1)

⇒ (1)/(y)+(1)/(z)=(1)/(21) (2)

⇒ As per the condition given, (1)/(x)=(2)/(z)

Putting the value in (1), and subtracting (2) from (1), we get

⇒ (2)/(z)+(1)/(y)-(1)/(z)-(1)/(y)=(1)/(14)-(1)/(21)

⇒ (1)/(z)=(3-2)/(42)=(1)/(42)

⇒ z = 42 days

Putting the value of z in equation (2), we get

⇒ (1)/(y)=(1)/(21)-(1)/(42)

⇒ (1)/(y)=(2-1)/(42)=(1)/(42)

⇒ y = 42 days

**Therefore, number of days in which Q alone can finish the work is 42 days.**

questions.question: O, T and P can do a piece of work in 3, 4 and 6 hours respectively. If they are working together, then in how much time they will finish the work?
questions.solution:

**Formula used:**

Work done = (1/Time taken)

**Solution:**

The LCM of 3, 4, and 6 is 12.

Work done by O in one hour = 1/3 × 12 = 4

Work done by T in one hour = 1/4 × 12 = 3

Work done by P in one hour = 1/6 × 12 = 2

Total work done in one hour = 4 + 3 + 2 = 9

Time taken to finish the work = 1/(Total work done in one hour)

= 12/9

= 4/3

= 1 + 1/3

= 1 hour and 20 minutes

**Therefore, when O, T, and P work together, they will finish the work in 1 hour and 20 minutes.**

questions.question: A and B can complete a piece of work in 15 days. B and C in 30 days and C and A in 45 days. In how many days will they complete the work if they start working together?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A and B can complete a piece of work in 15 days.

B and C can complete a piece of work in 30 days.

C and A can complete a piece of work in 45 days.

**Formula Used:**

Work rate of A + B + C = 1/(Work rate of A and B) + 1/(Work rate of B and C) + 1/(Work rate of C and A)

Time taken when A, B, and C work together = 1 / (Work rate of A + B + C)

**Calculation:**

Let the work rates of A, B, and C be A, B, and C respectively.

A + B = 1/15

B + C = 1/30

C + A = 1/45

Adding these three equations:

(A + B) + (B + C) + (C + A) = 1/15 + 1/30 + 1/45

⇒ 2A + 2B + 2C = 1/15 + 1/30 + 1/45

⇒ 2(A + B + C) = (6 + 3 + 2) / 90

⇒ 2(A + B + C) = 11 / 90

⇒ A + B + C = 11 / 180

Time taken when A, B, and C work together = 1 / (A + B + C)

⇒ Time = 1 / (11 / 180)

⇒ Time = 180 / 11

questions.question: 20 men can finish a work in 220 days, but at the end of 90 days, 20 additional men are employed. In how many more days will the work be completed?

Total work = Number of men X Total number of days

Total work = 20 x 220

Total work = 4400.

Work completed after 90 days = 20 x 90 

= 1800

Required work = 1800.

Remaining work = Total work - Work completed after 90 days.

= 4400 - 1800

= 2600.

Remaining work = Total men after new recruitment x X

2600 = 40 x X

X = (2600)/(40)

X = 65.

Thus, **Work will be completed after 65 more days.**

Thus, Work will be completed after 65 more days

Inverse Relation of Time and Efficiency

Time taken to complete a work is inversely proportional to the efficiency of the worker. Time = 1 ÷ Efficiency (keeping work constant).

Combined Work Formula

Work and Wages

questions.question: A alone can complete the project in 10 days; B alone can complete it in 20 days while C alone can complete it in 30 days. They together earn Rs. 1,100 for the project. By how much do the total earnings of A and C exceed the earnings of B?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Wage ratio = Inverse ratio of days taken = 1/10 : 1/20 : 1/30 = 6 : 3 : 2

Total ratio parts = 6 + 3 + 2 = 11 parts → Rs. 1100

1 part → Rs. 100

Required difference = (A + C) − B = (6 + 2) − 3 = 5 parts

Difference = 5 × 100 = Rs. 500

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 500.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Calculations:**

⇒ Ratio of efficiencies A : B : C = 6 : 3 : 2

⇒ Total efficiency parts = 6 + 3 + 2 = 11 parts

⇒ Earnings of A = (6 ÷ 11) × 1100 = Rs. 600

⇒ Earnings of B = (3 ÷ 11) × 1100 = Rs. 300

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Work and Wages

Wages are always distributed in proportion to the total work done by each individual. If individuals work together for the same number of days, their wages are divided exactly in the ratio of their one-day work (efficiencies).

Efficiency and Time Relation

Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken to complete the work. For instance, if the ratio of time taken by two people is A : B, their efficiency ratio is B : A.

Total Work Assumption

A highly effective way to determine total work is by calculating the Least Common Multiple (LCM) of the distinct days taken by all individuals to finish the task alone.
